problem: Consider a linear transformation $\,T\,.$ If $\,{v}_{1}+{v}_{2}=0\,$ and $\,T({v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}21 \\ 17 \\ -14\end{aligned}]\,$, find $\,T(37{v}_{1}+39{v}_{2}).$
worked_solution:
First, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}37{v}_{1}+39{v}_{2} & =37{v}_{1}+37{v}_{2}+2{v}_{2} \\  & =37({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})+2{v}_{2} \\  & =37(0)+2{v}_{2} \\  & =2{v}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
T(37{v}_{1}+39{v}_{2})=T(2{v}_{2}).
$$

 

Now, since $T$ is a linear transformation, we have that $T(kv)=kT(v).$ So 

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2{v}_{2}) & =2T({v}_{2}) \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}21 \\ 17 \\ -14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}42 \\ 34 \\ -28\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, $T(37{v}_{1}+39{v}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}42 \\ 34 \\ -28\end{aligned}].$
